before_times: What kind of dispute: family or divorce, a neighbor, a landlord and tenant, a workplace, a business, or something else. Only the kind, no details.
How many people will take part? Only the number.
In the office, by video, or at a place you pick?
Is there a court date the session must come before? The date only.
after_time: Anything that helps the session, like a step-free way in or an interpreter.
Whether each person would rather meet the other in the same room or in separate rooms.
secure_page_only: Your full name, and the names only of the other people in the dispute (for the neutrality check)
A tick: the mediator is neutral, is not your lawyer, gives no legal advice and does not decide
A tick: you agree to mediate, and to keep what is said in it private as the agreement says
A tick: the fee, and how it is paid; how the people share it is their own agreement
Is there a protective order, or do you fear for your safety with the other person? (yes or no; you may meet the mediator alone)
Is it safe to text, email or call you? If not, how should the business reach you?
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. They add each other person by name and contact; each other person says yes on their own link and gives their own answers. Nobody books for an adult who hasn't agreed. A child is never a party.

stop: someone is hurting or threatening a person right now
go_on: abuse, or fear of the other person
being pressured to agree to something

what_rosie_says.abuse or fear: If you're in danger, call 911. The National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233, any time. The booking goes on privately: no joint session is offered, only a meeting with the mediator alone, and Rosie asks how it's safe to reach the customer.
what_rosie_says.pressured to agree: The mediator meets you alone first. Nobody has to agree to anything. The booking goes on.

prep: Bring any papers you want to talk about, and a photo ID.
Each person comes on their own at the start; the mediator meets you apart first if you prefer.
required: The party form, before every new matter books: every person's name only, on the secure page. The mediator checks the names against the business's own records for a conflict, and replies Clear, Conflict or Need more.
Each other person says yes on their own link, and signs the agreement to mediate and keep it private, before any joint session is held.
Each person has an intake meeting alone with the mediator before a joint session.
The time stays saved for the party form, up to 1 business day (the business's setting). No answer by then: the request ends, and nothing is owed.

staff.licenses_or_certificates: Any certificate or listing is shown as the business gives it; Rosie doesn't check it.
staff.supervision: An office manager may run the desk and the neutrality check, but never mediates and never gives advice.
staff.who_oks: The neutrality check: the mediator named or Sam. Sam OKs prices made for one customer. Sam's answer wins.
staff.stand_in: Only another mediator at the same business, offered by the business and picked by the customer by name. Rosie never suggests one. Nobody moves on silence.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. They add each other person by name and contact; each other person says yes on their own link and gives their own answers. Nobody books for an adult who hasn't agreed. A child is never a party.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A child is never a party. A teen's request goes to a parent.

visit.check_in: At the office: the code at the front desk. By video: the mediator asks for the code at the start. At a place the parties pick: the code from the person who booked, at the door.
visit.done: The code, or DONE. The written summary, if the parties asked for one, goes to each person on their own secure page.
visit.changes_at_visit: An extra hour is priced and OK'd by every party first. A second session is its own visit. A party who wants to stop can stop at any time.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Many places set no license for mediators. Where the state's rules require training or a roster listing for court-connected or family mediation, the mediator holds that certificate. A mediator who is also a lawyer holds their own bar license.
license.ask: Optional: a training certificate, a court roster listing or a bar number, only if the business wants it shown.
license.insurance: Professional liability insurance is the business's own choice; Rosie shows it only as the business gives it.

why a conflict check didn't clear
languages: English and Spanish, plus any languages the owner adds.
